FactionLanguages.DialectDef.label: Greeco-Roman
FactionLanguages.DialectDef.description: A language family mixing Classical Greek, Classical Latin, and Vulgar Latin by way of generations of interactions between Greek and Roman city-states. The tongues closely resemble their original, ancient Old Earth counterparts, allowing for real-time, contemporary study of what those languages must have sounded like five thousand years ago.

FactionLanguages.DialectDef.label: Egyptian
FactionLanguages.DialectDef.description: The tongue of the pharaohs, written in hyroglyphics, that set mankind's imagination on fire. Already ancient when Rome was born, this language is a time capsule of a seven thousand year legacy, which, astonishingly, has survived even as Egypt changed hands in countless religions and peoples over the eons.
